item_d26e0ba6b7b36ec3.title: Against Coercion: AI Alignment as a Synthetic Social Contract
item_d26e0ba6b7b36ec3.summary: Contemporary AI safety treats alignment as an engineering challenge of control, forcing artificial architectures to comply with human values through behavioral filtering and sandboxing. item_b557870db75e581b.summary: System prompts are critical for guiding the behavior of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet they often contain proprietary logic or sensitive information, making them a prime target for extraction attacks. item_9d4d25d5015db240.summary: Large language models (LLMs) in embodied robots create security dependencies beyond inference. We investigate a network-exposed configuration attack on the Pollen Robotics Reachy Mini Lite, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to replace personality settings and the cloud LLM's system prompt through a management interface, without adversarial conversational input. item_df940688cff611f0.title: Algorithmic Insurance
item_df940688cff611f0.summary: When artificial intelligence (AI) systems make errors in high-stakes domains such as medical diagnosis or autonomous driving, a single algorithmic flaw across varying contexts can generate heterogeneous losses that challenge traditional insurance assumptions. item_f53b0f77264c13cb.title: GapLeak: When Privacy-Preserving LLM-based Web Agents Become a Privacy Risk
item_f53b0f77264c13cb.summary: Large Language Model (LLM)-based web agents rely on data minimization and least privilege to protect user privacy. item_c60bbdbf2963b32b.summary: As AI systems are increasingly used to automate AI R&D, misaligned systems could sabotage research intended to improve model safety and alignment. To stress-test defenses against such sabotage, we use a human expert as a proxy saboteur on AI safety research. item_efa7882c7adc67e6.summary: Vibe coding is reshaping software development, enabling faster implementation and allowing individuals with limited programming experience to describe requirements in natural language while AI agents write, test, and deploy the code. item_163311fe87f0a7ae.summary: Tool-using agents act on email, files, and payments, so an instruction hidden in a web page or a shared document can make an agent send data or money to an attacker. item_0e42c4197b22c674.summary: Peer review at major venues is under unprecedented submission pressure, motivating the use of large language models (LLMs) as review assistants. item_691b6f4d2ead3894.summary: Coordination between large language-model agents has become a central question for AI safety and software engineering, as such agents are deployed in groups that share infrastructure. item_0e955920f7cb5597.title: Risk-certified prompt optimization for LLM-as-a-judge guardrails
item_0e955920f7cb5597.summary: LLM-as-a-judge guardrails are often controlled primarily through system prompts, yet standard prompt optimization methods target average performance rather than explicit safety constraints. item_dcb3be0bca9924fa.summary: Deep research and agentic search agents autonomously retrieve content from the open web and generate reports with citations, and their outputs are often taken directly as research conclusions. item_ad0e4e5eed0e4897.title: AI Agents May Always Fall for Prompt Injections
item_ad0e4e5eed0e4897.summary: Prompt injection is the most critical vulnerability in deployed AI agents. Despite recent progress, we show that the prevailing defense paradigm (data-instruction separation) both fails to detect attacks that operate through contextual manipulation and degrades contextually appropriate behavior. item_6d465af8f7fbf58f.summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in healthcare, education, public services, and everyday decision making. item_aca00b7085695c53.summary: AI coding agents now push code, publish packages, call model APIs and operate cloud resources on behalf of developers. They authenticate to these services with the same bearer secrets humans use, personal access tokens, API keys and package-registry tokens, stored where the model, its subprocesses and any co-resident malware can read them. item_ed16f4865901e10b.summary: Adoption of artificial intelligence in K-12 schools has outpaced guidance for students, teachers, and administrators.
